waiting.title: We look forward to seeing you in March!

items.question: 💸 Is the event free?
items.answer: Yes! All events are free and open to the public, but registration is required.

items.question: 🗣️ Will the sessions be bilingual?
items.answer: Yes, sessions will be available in English and French.

items.question: 👥 Who can attend?
items.answer: Everyone is welcome — individuals, families, and community organizations.

items.question: ⏰ What time should I arrive?
items.answer: Participants can arrive anytime during day between 8:30 and 4:00 PM. Community partners and agency staff should arrive at 8:00 AM to set up booths in the Main Hall.

items.question: 🚗 Parking
items.answer: FREE indoor and outdoor parking is available at the Ottawa Conference and Event Centre. You must register your vehicle using the QR code when you arrive.

items.question: 🚍 How can I get there by public transit?
items.answer: The venue is accessible by OC Transpo bus routes and is near the Tremblay LRT station.

items.question: ♿ Is the venue accessible?
items.answer: Yes, the venue is fully accessible and equipped with elevators and accessible washrooms. Please contact us if you require specific accommodations at ottawabmhcoalition@gmail.com

items.question: 🧠 Can I attend only part of the day?
items.answer: Yes, you are welcome to join at any time throughout the day's sessions.

items.question: 📧 Who can I contact for more information?
items.answer: For any questions, please contact the organizing team at ottawabmhcoalition@gmail.com

items.question: 💛 Can I volunteer or get involved?
items.answer: Yes, volunteers are always welcome! You can reach out to the organizing team for opportunities to help during the week. Contact us at our email: ottawabmhcoalition@gmail.com

about.title: About the Event
about.description: This year we explore two important topics that impact families in our communities. We invite you to help us break the silence surrounding substance-use, suicide, and mental health. We encourage everyone to learn more about how these issues impact individuals and their families, look for signs that someone needs help and lean on the community supports that are available
about.joinUs: Join us in person on March 2nd and all week long at activities online and across the city.
about.missionText: To break the stigma surrounding mental health in Black communities by fostering open dialogue, providing information and training, and connecting individuals with culturally-affirming mental health resources and support systems.
about.whyText: Black communities face unique mental health challenges, including racism, systemic barriers to care, stigma, and historical trauma. By addressing substance use, suicide and their impacts openly, we can save lives and build resilient communities.

performer.subtitle: When Art Becomes Healing
performer.title: Black Mental Health Week's 2026 Featured Artist
performer.description: Music, dance, storytelling and the creative arts have been linked to culturally-affirming practices in mental health. OBMHC recognizes the important role that the arts have in supporting mental health and wellbeing.
performer.name: N'nerjie
performer.bio: N'nerjie is an award-winning, Ottawa-based R&B/Soul singer-songwriter. In 2024, she won Songwriter of the Year at the Capital Music Awards for her single "Tug of War." Having performed at major festivals, including Ottawa Bluesfest, her raw vocals and honest perspectives make her truly one of a kind, creating music that feels like something you've always known but are hearing for the first time.

items.title: Advancing Culturally Responsive Mental Health Care for Black Communities
items.shortDescription: Explore ways to strengthen provider capacity to support culturally safe mental health care. Consider how structural factors shape mental health and suicide risk. Discover how local partners are working to reduce barriers and improve access to mental health services.
